title: Seat the R20 carrier
instruction: Lay the two-pocket R20 floor sample flat. Match the wider carrier key to the wider pocket and lower both feet together.
facing: Pockets up, posts pointing sideways, long arm ends overhanging the sample.
check: Look edge-on. Both shoulders should touch at once without rocking.

title: Try A2 on the carrier
instruction: Slip the two diagonal holes over the pins until all four corners rest directly on the carrier seats. Touch opposite corners lightly.
facing: Central chip and both sockets toward the seats. The row of six fine holes runs along the floor edge.
check: Record any rock, binding or contact at the chip or sockets. Lift A2 off and set the R20 fixture aside.

title: Orient the open housing
instruction: Lay the unpowered plate-1 housing on the bench, open side up. Set the matching plate-2 bezel aside until closure.
facing: Reel to the right (+X), USB to the left (−X), power key at the top (+Y), service cover at the bottom (−Y).
check: Find the four sensor lands on the inner face of the reel wall and the two pins at diagonally opposite corners.

title: Identify the A2 sensor face
instruction: Find the central chip between two taller sockets. Hold this face toward the reel.
facing: The six wiring holes form a row along the edge nearest the floor.
check: Identify all four corner holes before offering the board to the shell.

title: Shim the four A2 lands
instruction: Measure four removable 0.25 mm shims. Place one on each circular land inside the right wall. Slotted stock can straddle the two locating pins.
facing: Each shim goes between a land and the component-side face of the board.
check: All four lands have a bearing surface. Both pins project through the shim plane, and the chip and socket spaces are clear.

title: Seat A2 against the reel wall
instruction: Lower A2 into the right-hand bay and slide it toward the reel over the two diagonal pins.
facing: Six wiring holes down. Central chip toward the axle, with the two sockets flanking it.
check: The board lies parallel to the wall on all four shims. Check for rocking and binding.

title: Place the two A3 floor strips
instruction: Measure both long strips to 2.10 mm high. Lay them flat in the haptic bay with centers 8.00 mm apart.
facing: Run their 12 mm lengths from the service edge toward the power key.
check: In installed coordinates the strip centers are at (18, −6) and (26, −6) mm. Both should rest flat on the floor.

title: Set A3 on both strips
instruction: Center the haptic gauge on the two strips. Its right edge is 16.20 mm inboard of the reel wall plane, and its top edge is 3.20 mm past the axle centerline toward the power key.
facing: Components up, tall J1 header toward the lower service edge.
check: A3 rests flat at Z4.60 mm. Check clearance above J1 again when the display is seated.

title: Locate the KEY switch board
instruction: Set the 11 × 10 mm KEY gauge upright in the pocket beneath the top-left power cap.
facing: Long edge left to right, fixed switch plunger toward the top edge (+Y).
check: Look from above and check that the plunger lines up with the cap opening.

title: Fit the retainer and power cap
instruction: Seat the west retainer over the board, then offer the power cap to the fixed plunger.
facing: Retainer at the left end of the board, cap on the top edge.
check: The board stays located and the cap is captured. The printed switch represents its unpressed position.

title: Identify the USB1 indicator
instruction: Pick up USB-PCB1, the 4.80 × 3.20 mm indicator card. Locate the raised LED block in the middle of one face.
facing: Turn the LED toward the left wall (−X) before fitting the card.
check: Its long edge will run from the service edge toward the power key.

title: Slide USB1 into the guides
instruction: Lower the indicator between the two guides inside the left wall until its bottom edge reaches the shelf.
facing: LED block faces the U light guide. The 4.80 mm edge runs along the wall in plan.
check: Check that USB1 sits square on its shelf. The nominal LED-to-guide gap is 0.30 mm.

title: Try one inert battery gauge
instruction: Choose one plate-6 battery gauge and lower its broad face onto the bay supports. The two pack gauges are tested separately.
facing: Wire sockets or wire stubs toward the power-key edge (+Y).
check: Check the pack sits level with its wire end clear. Record which gauge is in the housing.

title: Seat the battery bridge
instruction: Lower the plate-2 wire bridge onto its mounting lands over the inert gauge.
facing: The bridge spans the pack near the wire end.
check: The bridge rests on its lands. Check that the pack clears the bridge and the mounting lands.

title: Turn A1 glass-face down
instruction: Lay A1 on a clean, soft surface. Find the USB-C shell and J8 on the exposed underside. Set out the two groups of three square spacers.
facing: Glass against the pad, bosses and connectors up. Use the USB-C shell to identify the end that fits the left opening.
check: The underside view reverses left and right. Keep the reel-side ends of A4 and A5 aligned.

title: Place the three A4 spacers
instruction: Use three 3 × 3 mm blocks, each 2.465 mm high. From A4’s −X/−Y corner in installed plan, the centers are (2.50, 2.00), (20.50, 2.50) and (20.50, 10.50) mm.
facing: A4 spans X13 to 36 and Y−12 to 1 mm in installed plan, on the reel side toward the service edge.
check: Measure between bearing faces. If the printed heights differ, record them and use calibrated stock for a nominal-height trial.

title: Rest A4 on the short spacers
instruction: Place the 23 × 13 mm integration board on its three spacers. Set its reel-side edge 3.01 mm inboard of A1’s PCB edge.
facing: Plain back toward A1, component blocks toward the housing floor.
check: Press lightly over each support. Check that the board sits level and all three blocks remain under it.

title: Place the three A5 spacers
instruction: Use three 3 × 3 mm blocks, each 3.160 mm high. From A5’s −X/−Y corner in installed plan, the centers are (4.50, 13.50), (15.50, 11.10) and (19.50, 14.30) mm.
facing: A5 spans X13 to 36 and Y3 to 19 mm in installed plan, beside A4 toward the power key.
check: Measure all three blocks. The stated height includes the full dry support stack. Keep the bearing faces free of adhesive.

title: Rest A5 on the tall spacers
instruction: Place the 23 × 16 mm power board on its three spacers and align its reel-side edge with A4.
facing: Plain back toward A1, component blocks toward the housing floor.
check: Leave a 2.00 mm gap between A4 and A5. Check that A5 contacts each spacer and sits level.

title: Identify the USB2 resistor
instruction: Pick up USB-PCB2, the 3.20 × 2.00 mm card. Find its single raised resistor.
facing: The resistor faces the display (+Z) when installed.
check: The flat back faces the housing floor.

title: Position USB2 beside J8
instruction: Hold the resistor card by its edge beside A1’s J8 connector. Its installed footprint is X−22.60 to −19.40 mm and Y17 to 19 mm.
facing: Resistor toward the display, long edge across the housing.
check: The flat back is at Z17.60 mm. Check this card separately if temporary retention would interfere with closure.

title: Lower the display onto its four seats
instruction: Support A4, A5, their spacers and USB2 as you turn A1 over. Lower the stack onto all four mounting datums.
facing: Glass up, USB-C shell toward the left opening, lower switches toward the service cover.
check: A1 rests evenly with its holes unloaded. Reopen and restore any shifted gauge or spacer before checking closure.

title: Fit the bezel and inspect the seam
instruction: Lower the matching plate-2 bezel evenly by hand. If an edge lifts, photograph it with the parts still seated. Record the edge, gap, spacer heights and battery gauge.
facing: Screen opening over the glass, USB cutout toward the left.
check: Lift the bezel and remove the suspected gauge to isolate contact. Repeat closure with the other inert pack gauge.
checklist: The bezel seam is even and there is daylight around the glass. The nominal glass-to-rim gap is 0.25 mm.
The USB-C shell clears the opening and bezel. Use the solid gauge for the outer trim check only.
The lower switches line up with the service cover. KEY remains captured and A2 stays on all four shims.
A3’s tall header clears the display stack. Each battery gauge clears the bridge in its own closure trial.
After disassembly, count eight board gauges, eight printed spacers and the four removable A2 shims.
